request: We need an app for staff to check attendees in at the venue entrance on the event day.

problem.value: Replace slow/error-prone manual entry control with a fast, reliable on-site check-in so staff can identify and admit attendees quickly at the door.
problem.evidence: "an app for staff to check attendees in at the venue entrance on the event day"

actors.value: On-site staff/hostess operate the scanning; attendees are the subjects checked in; an event manager likely oversees; security may be involved for access control.

business_objects.value: Attendee, Check-in, Event are implied; the origin of the expected-attendee list (import from registration, live edits, walk-ins) is not stated.
business_objects.evidence: request names "attendees" but not where the list comes from

workflow.value: Likely: staff scans/searches attendee → marks arrived. Whether a second scan means duplicate, re-entry, or a different zone/session is unspecified.
workflow.evidence: "check attendees in" implies a single-step action, but the model behind it is unstated

integrations.value: Unknown whether the app must work offline (local snapshot + sync) or can rely on online connectivity at the venue.

permissions.value: Staff perform check-ins; unclear if different staff are scoped to specific entrances/zones or all see the full list.

config_vs_custom.value: Unclear whether this is a one-off build for a single event or the first instance of a reusable multi-event kit.

constraints.value: Fixed, non-movable event date; app must work reliably during a short live window with no fallback sprint.

edge_cases.value: Not addressed: duplicate scans, poor connectivity, unreadable badges/QR, walk-ins, name mismatches, concurrent multi-door scanning.

reporting.value: Post-event attendance data (who came, when, where) is typically a client deliverable, but not mentioned yet.

risks.value: Check-in path failing on event day is the top operational risk; no fallback or rehearsal plan mentioned.

questions.q: Where does the expected-attendee list come from (an import from a registration system?), and can staff add walk-ins or correct names on the spot the day of the event?
questions.why: uncertainty(high, empty) × impact(high): the upstream source of the attendee list determines the whole data model and whether on-site registration is in scope — a blind spot that changes build size significantly.

questions.q: Does the app need to work without reliable venue wifi/4G (offline, with check-ins syncing later), or can we assume solid connectivity at the entrance?
questions.why: uncertainty(high, empty) × impact(high): offline vs. online-only is an architectural decision, not a setting, and venues frequently have dead zones — getting this wrong risks the app failing live.

questions.q: When the same attendee is scanned a second time, what should happen — block it as a duplicate, allow it as re-entry, or record it as access to a different zone/session?
questions.why: uncertainty(high, empty) × impact(high): this single behaviour decides the check-in data model (one record per attendee vs. many) and is the first thing that breaks if assumed rather than confirmed.

questions.q: Is this app being built for this single event only, or should it be designed as a reusable kit for future events?
questions.why: uncertainty(high, empty) × impact(high): a throwaway build and a multi-event platform differ in data model, configurability and cost — worth settling before any design work.

questions.q: Will multiple staff scan simultaneously at different entrances/zones, and do they need different access (e.g. staff at Zone A can't check in Zone B)?
questions.why: uncertainty(high, empty) × impact(high): concurrent scanning across doors is where naive builds first break (same attendee processed twice within seconds) and it also shapes the permission model.

questions.q: What's the expected volume and peak arrival window (e.g. most attendees arriving in the 20 minutes before the keynote)?
questions.why: uncertainty(medium-high, inferred) × impact(high): throughput is a functional spec here — a 3-second flow and a 15-second flow are different products at the door, and this is rarely stated upfront.

summary.objective: Give on-site staff a fast, reliable way to identify and record attendee arrivals at the venue entrance on the day of the event.
summary.scope: Likely includes: a staff-facing check-in app (scan/search attendee), a local or synced copy of the expected-attendee list, marking arrivals, and some visibility/export of who checked in. Exact scope depends on list origin, offline needs, and single-event vs. reusable-kit ambition.
assumptions: Staff are the primary operators, checking attendees in against an expected list (not yet confirmed how that list arrives or is maintained).
The event has a fixed, non-movable date, making a manual fallback and on-site rehearsal part of the implicit scope.
A single scan/search-then-mark-arrived workflow is assumed, though duplicate/re-entry/zone semantics are unconfirmed.
Some form of post-event attendance reporting is expected even though not explicitly requested.
summary.blind_spot: The request describes the check-in action itself but not where the attendee list comes from, whether the app must survive venue connectivity gaps, or what a second scan of the same person should mean — any one of these silently expands scope from a simple scanning screen into a full offline-sync, multi-entrance system.

problem.evidence: "app for staff to check attendees in at the venue entrance" — no stated pain point, but the ask implies manual check-in is too slow or unreliable today.

current_process.evidence: Not stated — unknown whether there is an existing registration list, a paper backup, or a prior tool being replaced.

success_metrics.evidence: Not stated. In event-ops, throughput (seconds/attendee at peak) is a functional spec, not a nice-to-have — default impact raised from medium to high.

business_rules.evidence: Not stated: duplicate scan vs re-entry vs different-zone access, and concurrent scans across multiple entrance devices, are unresolved.

questions.why: uncertainty(empty) × impact(high): this single behaviour choice changes the data model (one check-in per attendee vs. many events per attendee) and is the first thing that breaks with naive multi-device use.

questions.why: uncertainty(empty) × impact(high, raised from default): throughput at the door is a functional requirement in event ops, not a nice-to-have — it determines the UI flow and identification method (scan vs. manual search).

briefs.solution: A staff-operated check-in app that identifies attendees against an expected list and records arrivals at the venue entrance.

challenges.headline: Connectivity assumed, not confirmed
challenges.premise: The check-in app is being scoped without stating whether venue connectivity can be relied on.
challenges.alternative: Design the check-in flow around a local snapshot of the attendee list with deferred sync, confirmed against the actual venue's connectivity before committing to an architecture, rather than defaulting to always-online.
challenges.consequence: Building online-only and discovering dead zones on event day turns the one path that must not fail into a visible queue at the door, with no time left to fix it.
challenges.recommendation: Get a real connectivity read at the venue, or default to offline-first, before architecture decisions are locked.

challenges.headline: Second scan meaning undefined
challenges.premise: The workflow assumes a single scan-then-mark-arrived action, with no definition of what a repeat scan of the same attendee means.
challenges.alternative: Model duplicate (block), re-entry (allow) and zone/session access (separate record) as three distinct outcomes agreed with the client, since one attendee can legitimately produce several check-in events.
challenges.consequence: Shipping a single boolean check-in state forces a data-model rebuild the moment re-entry or multi-zone access shows up on the day.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether the event has multiple zones/sessions or re-entry scenarios before finalizing the data model.

challenges.headline: Single-event vs reusable kit
challenges.premise: The build is implicitly scoped as a one-off app for this event, with no explicit decision on reusability.
challenges.alternative: Settle explicitly whether this is a throwaway build or the first instance of a multi-event kit — it changes the data model, the configuration layer and the cost baseline from day one.
challenges.consequence: Building single-event-only and later needing a second event forces a retrofit of the whole configuration model; over-engineering for reuse on a one-off wastes budget against a fixed deadline.
challenges.recommendation: Ask the client directly whether more events are planned and price the two paths separately.

decisions.decision: Check-in is staff-operated at the entrance, not attendee self-service.

decisions.alternative: Self-service scanning at a kiosk or turnstile.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires staffing every entrance, in exchange for the judgment and fallback capacity a scanner-only flow can't provide.
